verses.zh: 摩西将以色列众人召了来，对他们说：「以色列人哪，我今日晓谕你们的律例典章，你们要听，可以学习，谨守遵行。
verses.en: Then Moses called all the people of Israel together and said to them:[NOTE:1] “Listen, Israel, to the statutes and ordinances that I am about to deliver to you today; learn them and be careful to keep them!
notes: Heb “and Moses called to all Israel and he said to them”; NAB, NASB, NIV “Moses summoned (convened NRSV) all Israel.”

verses.zh: 耶和华―我们的　神在何烈山与我们立约。
verses.en: The Lord our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.

verses.zh: 这约不是与我们列祖立的，乃是与我们今日在这里存活之人立的。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] did not make this covenant with our ancestors[NOTE:2] but with us, we who are here today, all of us living now.
notes: Heb “the Lord.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.
Heb “fathers.”

verses.zh: 耶和华在山上，从火中，面对面与你们说话―
verses.en: The Lord spoke face to face with you at the mountain, from the middle of the fire.

verses.zh: 那时我站在耶和华和你们中间，要将耶和华的话传给你们；因为你们惧怕那火，没有上山―说：
verses.en: (I was standing between the Lord and you at that time to reveal the Lord’s message to you, because you were afraid of the fire and would not go up the mountain.) He said:

verses.zh: 「『我是耶和华―你的　神，曾将你从埃及地为奴之家领出来。
verses.en: “I am the Lord your God—he who brought you from the land of Egypt, from the place of slavery.

verses.zh: 「『除了我以外，你不可有别的神。
verses.en: “You must not have any other gods[NOTE:1] besides me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “there must not be for you other gods.” The expression “for you” indicates possession.

Heb “upon my face,” or “before me” (עַל־פָּנָיַ, ʿal panaya). Some understand this in a locative sense: “in my sight.” The translation assumes that the phrase indicates exclusion. The idea is that of placing any other god before the Lord in the sense of taking his place. Contrary to the view of some, this does not leave the door open for a henotheistic system where the Lord is the primary god among others. In its literary context the statement must be taken in a monotheistic sense. See, e.g., 4:39; 6:13-15.

verses.zh: 「『不可为自己雕刻偶像，也不可做甚么形像，彷佛上天、下地和地底下、水中的百物。
verses.en: “You must not make for yourself an image[NOTE:1] of anything in heaven above, on earth below, or in the waters beneath.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “an image, any likeness.”
Heb “under the earth” (so ASV, NASB, NRSV); NCV “below the land.”

verses.zh: 不可跪拜那些像，也不可事奉它，因为我耶和华―你的　神是忌邪的　神。恨我的，我必追讨他的罪，自父及子，直到三、四代；
verses.en: You must not worship or serve them, for I, the Lord your God, am a jealous God. I punish[NOTE:1] the sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons for the sin of the fathers who reject[NOTE:2] me,[NOTE:3]
notes: In the Hebrew text the form is a participle, which is subordinated to what precedes. For the sake of English style, the translation divides this lengthy verse into two sentences.

Heb “who hate” (so NAB, NIV, NLT). Just as “to love” (אָהֵב, ʾahev) means in a covenant context “to choose, obey,” so “to hate” (שָׂנֵא, saneʾ) means “to reject, disobey” (cf. the note on the word “loved” in Deut 4:37; see also 5:10).

Heb “visiting the sin of fathers upon sons and upon a third (generation) and upon a fourth (generation) of those who hate me.” God sometimes punishes children for the sins of a father (cf. Num 16:27, 32; Josh 7:24-25; 2 Sam 21:1-9). On the principle of corporate solidarity and responsibility in OT thought see J. Kaminsky, Corporate Responsibility in the Hebrew Bible (JSOTSup). In the idiom of the text, the father is the first generation and the “sons” the second generation, making grandsons the third and great-grandsons the fourth. The reference to a third and fourth generation is a way of emphasizing that the sinner’s punishment would last throughout his lifetime. In this culture, where men married and fathered children at a relatively young age, it would not be unusual for one to see his great-grandsons. In an Aramaic tomb inscription from Nerab dating to the seventh century b.c., Agbar observes that he was surrounded by “children of the fourth generation” as he lay on his death bed (see ANET 661). The language of the text differs from Exod 34:7, the sons are the first generation, the grandsons (literally, “sons of the sons”) the second, great-grandsons the third, and great-great-grandsons the fourth. One could argue that formulation in Deut 5:9 (see also Exod 20:5) is elliptical/abbreviated or that the text suffers from an accidental scribal omission (the repetition of the words “sons” would invite accidental omission).

verses.zh: 爱我、守我诫命的，我必向他们发慈爱，直到千代。
verses.en: but I show covenant faithfulness[NOTE:1] to the thousands[NOTE:2] who choose[NOTE:3] me and keep my commandments.
notes: This theologically rich term (חֶסֶד, khesed) describes God’s loyalty to those who keep covenant with him. Sometimes it is used synonymously with בְּרִית (berit, “covenant”; Deut 7:9), and sometimes interchangeably with it (Deut 7:12). See H.-J. Zobel, TDOT 5:44-64.

Another option is to understand this as referring to “thousands (of generations) of those who love me” (cf. NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT). See Deut 7:9. tc By a slight emendation (לֲאַלֻּפִים [laʾallufim] for לַאֲלָפִים [laʾalafim]) “clans” could be read in place of the MT reading “thousands.” However, no ms or versional evidence exists to support this emendation.
Heb “love.” See note on the word “reject” in v. 9.

verses.zh: 「『不可妄称耶和华―你　神的名；因为妄称耶和华名的，耶和华必不以他为无罪。
verses.en: “You must not make use of the name of the Lord your God for worthless purposes,[NOTE:1] for the Lord will not exonerate anyone who abuses his name that way.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “take up the name of the Lord your God to emptiness”; KJV “take the name of the Lord thy God in vain.” The idea here is not cursing or profanity in the modern sense of these terms, but rather the use of the divine Name for unholy, mundane purposes, that is, for meaningless (Hebrew שָׁוְא [shavʾ]) and empty ends. In ancient Israel this would include using the Lord’s name as a witness in vows one did not intend to keep.
Heb “who takes up his name to emptiness.”

verses.zh: 「『当照耶和华―你　神所吩咐的守安息日为圣日。
verses.en: “Be careful to observe[NOTE:1] the Sabbath day just as the Lord your God has commanded you.
notes: Heb “to make holy,” that is, to put to special use, in this case, to sacred purposes (cf. vv. 13-15).

verses.zh: 六日要劳碌做你一切的工，
verses.en: You are to work and do all your tasks in six days,

verses.zh: 但第七日是向耶和华―你　神当守的安息日。这一日，你和你的儿女、仆婢、牛、驴、牲畜，并在你城里寄居的客旅，无论何工都不可做，使你的仆婢可以和你一样安息。
verses.en: but the seventh day is the Sabbath[NOTE:1] of the Lord your God. On that day you must not do any work, you, your son, your daughter, your male slave, your female slave, your ox, your donkey, any other animal, or the resident foreigner who lives with you,[NOTE:2] so that your male and female slaves, like yourself, may have rest.
notes: There is some degree of paronomasia (wordplay) here: “the seventh (הַשְּׁבִיעִי, hasheviʿi) day is the Sabbath (שַׁבָּת, shabbat).” Otherwise, the words have nothing in common, since “Sabbath” is derived from the verb שָׁבַת (shavat, “to cease”).
Heb “in your gates”; NRSV, CEV “in your towns”; TEV “in your country.”

verses.zh: 你也要记念你在埃及地作过奴仆；耶和华―你　神用大能的手和伸出来的膀臂将你从那里领出来。因此，耶和华―你的　神吩咐你守安息日。
verses.en: Recall that you were slaves in the land of Egypt and that the Lord your God brought you out of there by strength and power.[NOTE:1] That is why the Lord your God has commanded you to observe[NOTE:2] the Sabbath day.
notes: Heb “by a strong hand and an outstretched arm,” the hand and arm symbolizing divine activity and strength. Cf. NLT “with amazing power and mighty deeds.”
Or “keep” (so KJV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 「『当照耶和华―你　神所吩咐的孝敬父母，使你得福，并使你的日子在耶和华―你　神所赐你的地上得以长久。
verses.en: “Honor[NOTE:1] your father and your mother just as the Lord your God has commanded you to do, so that your days may be extended and that it may go well with you in the land that he[NOTE:2] is about to give you.
notes: The imperative here means, literally, “regard as heavy” (כַּבֵּד, kabbed). The meaning is that great importance must be ascribed to parents by their children.
Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “He” in 5:3.

verses.zh: 「『不可杀人。
verses.en: “You must not murder.[NOTE:1]
notes: Traditionally “kill” (so KJV, ASV, RSV, NAB). The verb here (רָצַח, ratsakh) is generic for homicide but in the OT both killing in war and capital punishment were permitted and even commanded (Deut 13:5, 9; 20:13, 16-17), so the technical meaning here is “murder.”

verses.zh: 「『不可奸淫。
verses.en: “You must not commit adultery.

verses.zh: 「『不可偷盗。
verses.en: “You must not steal.

verses.zh: 「『不可作假见证陷害人。
verses.en: “You must not offer false testimony against another.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “your neighbor.” Clearly this is intended generically, however, and not to be limited only to those persons who live nearby (frequently the way “neighbor” is understood in contemporary contexts). So also in v. 20.

verses.zh: 「『不可贪恋人的妻子；也不可贪图人的房屋、田地、仆婢、牛、驴，并他一切所有的。』
verses.en: You must not desire[NOTE:1] another man’s[NOTE:2] wife, nor should you crave his[NOTE:3] house, his field, his male and female servants, his ox, his donkey, or anything else he owns.”[NOTE:4]
notes: The Hebrew verb used here (חָמַד, khamad) is different from the one translated “crave” (אָוַה, ʾavah) in the next line. The former has sexual overtones (“lust” or the like; cf. Song of Sol 2:3) whereas the latter has more the idea of a desire or craving for material things.
Heb “your neighbor’s.” See note on the term “fellow man” in v. 19.
Heb “your neighbor’s.” The pronoun is used in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “or anything that is your neighbor’s.”

verses.zh: 「这些话是耶和华在山上，从火中、云中、幽暗中，大声晓谕你们全会众的；此外并没有添别的话。他就把这话写在两块石版上，交给我了。」
verses.en: The Lord said these things to your entire assembly at the mountain from the middle of the fire, the cloud, and the darkness with a loud voice, and that was all he said.[NOTE:1] Then he inscribed the words[NOTE:2] on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
notes: Heb “and he added no more” (so KJV, NASB, NRSV); NLT “This was all he said at that time.”
Heb “them”; the referent (the words spoken by the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 「那时，火焰烧山，你们听见从黑暗中出来的声音；你们支派中所有的首领和长老都来就近我，
verses.en: Then, when you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness while the mountain was ablaze, all your tribal leaders and elders approached me.

verses.zh: 说：『看哪，耶和华―我们　神将他的荣光和他的大能显给我们看，我们又听见他的声音从火中出来。今日我们得见　神与人说话，人还存活。
verses.en: You said, “The Lord our God has shown us his great glory,[NOTE:1] and we have heard him speak from the middle of the fire. It is now clear to us[NOTE:2] that God can speak to human beings and they can keep on living.
notes: Heb “his glory and his greatness.”
Heb “this day we have seen.”

verses.zh: 现在这大火将要烧灭我们，我们何必冒死呢？若再听见耶和华―我们　神的声音就必死亡。
verses.en: But now, why should we die, because this intense fire will consume us? If we keep hearing the voice of the Lord our God we will die!

verses.zh: 凡属血气的，曾有何人听见永生　神的声音从火中出来，像我们听见还能存活呢？
verses.en: Who is there from the entire human race[NOTE:1] who has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the middle of the fire as we have, and has lived?
notes: Heb “who is there of all flesh.”

verses.zh: 求你近前去，听耶和华―我们　神所要说的一切话，将他对你说的话都传给我们，我们就听从遵行。』
verses.en: You go near so that you can hear everything the Lord our God is saying and then you can tell us whatever he[NOTE:1] says to you; then we will pay attention and do it.”
notes: Heb “the Lord our God.” See note on “He” in 5:3.

verses.zh: 「你们对我说的话，耶和华都听见了。耶和华对我说：『这百姓的话，我听见了；他们所说的都是。
verses.en: When the Lord heard you speaking to me, he[NOTE:1] said to me, “I have heard what these people have said to you—they have spoken well.
notes: Heb “the Lord.” See note on “He” in 5:3.

verses.zh: 惟愿他们存这样的心敬畏我，常遵守我的一切诫命，使他们和他们的子孙永远得福。
verses.en: If only it would really be their desire to fear me and obey[NOTE:1] all my commandments in the future, so that it may go well with them and their descendants forever.
notes: Heb “keep” (so KJV, NAB, NIV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 你去对他们说：你们回帐棚去吧！
verses.en: Go and tell them, ‘Return to your tents!’

verses.zh: 至于你，可以站在我这里，我要将一切诫命、律例、典章传给你；你要教训他们，使他们在我赐他们为业的地上遵行。』
verses.en: But as for you, remain here with me so I can declare to you all the commandments,[NOTE:1] statutes, and ordinances that you are to teach them, so that they can carry them out in the land I am about to give them.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “commandment.” The MT actually has the singular (הַמִּצְוָה, hammitsvah), suggesting perhaps that the following terms (חֻקִּים [khuqqim] and מִשְׁפָּטִים [mishpatim]) are in epexegetical apposition to “commandment.” That is, the phrase could be translated “the entire command, namely, the statutes and ordinances.” This would essentially make מִצְוָה (mitsvah) synonymous with תּוֹרָה (torah), the usual term for the whole collection of law.
Heb “to possess it” (so KJV, ASV); NLT “as their inheritance.”

verses.zh: 所以，你们要照耶和华―你们　神所吩咐的谨守遵行，不可偏离左右。
verses.en: Be careful, therefore, to do exactly what the Lord your God has commanded you; do not turn right or left!

verses.zh: 耶和华―你们　神所吩咐你们行的，你们都要去行，使你们可以存活得福，并使你们的日子在所要承受的地上得以长久。」
verses.en: Walk just as he[NOTE:1] has commanded you so that you may live, that it may go well with you, and that you may live long[NOTE:2] in the land you are going to possess.
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.
Heb “may prolong your days”; NAB “may have long life”; TEV “will continue to live.”
